newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to market hybrid cars in Europe, in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to market hybrid cars in Europe, in U.S.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday it hopes to launch hybrid cars, powered by a small engine and an electric motor, in the United States and Europe as soon as possible after their launch in Japan, due by the end of this year.

Toyota executive vice president Akihiro Wada said the firm hopes to introduce hybrid cars in the U.S. and Europe as soon as possible after their launch in Japan and after it had confirmed the reliability of the car in Japan.

Toyota has said hybrid cars are expected to reduce both fuel consumption and emissions of carbon dioxide by 50 percent compared with its existing gasoline-powered Corolla model and also reduce other emissions to one-tenth those of the Corolla.

Asked about the site for Toyota's second manufacturing plant in Europe, Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda said the company was still studying the site. He said there was no change since its previous statement that it expected to make an announcement at the end of this year or early next year.
Okuda said that compared with last year, Toyota's vehicle exports to the United States in 1997 were expected to be flat to five percent higher.

Asked about the effect of Japan's decontrol of foreign exchange transactions, to be effective from April next year, Okuda said Toyota could expect some savings on commission payments for foreign exchange dealings. Apart from that, the company was still studying the matter.
